title: Repeat buyers
summary: How many customers come back, and are they worth a loyalty program?

exec.note: needs this before Monday's budget review

brief: We grew fast in 2017, but I keep hearing most customers never come back. Before I fund a loyalty program, tell me how many customers actually bought twice, and what they're worth compared to everyone else.
deliver: Number of repeat customers, and average spend per repeat vs one-time customer.

parts.ask: How many unique customers do we have?
parts.solution: SELECT count(DISTINCT customer_unique_id) AS unique_customers FROM customers
parts.win: Good. That's the base I'll measure everything against.

parts.ask: How many of them placed more than one order?
parts.solution: SELECT count(*) AS repeat_customers FROM (SELECT c.customer_unique_id FROM customers c JOIN orders o USING (customer_id) GROUP BY 1 HAVING count(*) > 1)
parts.win: Small, but real. Now tell me what they're worth.

parts.ask: Average spend per customer (sum of item price, no freight) for repeat vs one-time customers. Customers with no items count as 0. Label the groups `Repeat` and `One Time`.
parts.solution: WITH per_customer AS (SELECT c.customer_unique_id, count(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS orders, coalesce(sum(i.price), 0) AS spend FROM customers c JOIN orders o USING (customer_id) LEFT JOIN order_items i USING (order_id) GROUP BY 1) SELECT CASE WHEN orders > 1 THEN 'Repeat' ELSE 'One Time' END AS customer_type, round(avg(spend), 2) AS avg_spend FROM per_customer GROUP BY 1
parts.win: Repeat customers spend almost twice as much. That's the case for the loyalty program.
